questions.title: Wallachia and Moldavia before 1878
questions.question: Should Wallachia, Moldavia and the United Principalities show as their own states before 1878?
questions.problem: OHM and Cliopatria show self-governing principalities. CShapes counts only fully independent states, so it shows the Ottoman Empire until 1878.
questions.conf_note: The facts are not in doubt; which map to show is a rule decision.
why: CShapes records only fully independent states.
Brăila was an Ottoman fortress until the Treaty of Adrianople (1829) returned it to Wallachia; CShapes and Cliopatria draw it coarsely.

questions.title: Russian and Austrian occupations of the principalities
questions.question: Should the "actual control" map show the foreign occupations of Wallachia and Moldavia?
questions.problem: CShapes and Cliopatria show Russia (1828–34, 1848–55) and Austria (1856) as holders; OHM keeps the principalities throughout.

actual.note: Russian and Ottoman troops after the 1848 revolutions
Russian occupation at the start of the Crimean War

questions.conf_note: The occupations are well documented, but the month each began and ended needs checking by someone who knows the period.
why: OHM records legal title only.
Cliopatria and CShapes mix legal title and military occupation, and use whole years.

questions.title: Serbia 1833–1878
questions.question: Should self-governing Serbia show as its own state before its independence in 1878?
questions.problem: OHM and Cliopatria show Serbia as its own state; CShapes shows the Ottoman Empire until 1878.
questions.conf_note: Only the rule decides this one.
why: CShapes records only fully independent states.

questions.title: When does self-governing Serbia begin?
questions.question: Did Serbia govern itself from 1815, from 1830, or only from 1833 as OHM has it?
questions.problem: OHM starts self-governing Serbia in 1833, Cliopatria before 1816, and CShapes only at independence in 1878.

legal.note: Ottoman sovereignty throughout; Serbian self-rule recognized in 1830

actual.note: Core districts around Belgrade: self-governing after the Second Serbian Uprising (1815)
Negotin, Zaječar and Kruševac: added to Serbia only in 1833

questions.conf_note: Historians date Serbian self-rule differently (1815, 1817, 1830). An expert should pick the date and check which districts it covered.
why: OHM uses the 1833 borders for the whole period.
Cliopatria extends early Serbia too far south (see the Niš question).

questions.title: Niš, Prokuplje and Kuršumlija before 1878
questions.question: Were Niš, Prokuplje and Kuršumlija Serbian before 1878?
questions.problem: Cliopatria places these towns in Serbia from 1816. OHM and CShapes keep them Ottoman until 1878.

legal.note: Taken by Serbia in January 1878, confirmed at Berlin

questions.conf_note: Both change dates come from the war record and the Treaty of Berlin.
why: Cliopatria draws early Serbia too large.

questions.title: Bulgaria after 1885 is missing from OHM
questions.question: Who held Bulgaria from the 1885 unification to 1900?
questions.problem: OHM ends its Bulgaria record in September 1885 and shows plain Ottoman territory afterward. CShapes and Cliopatria show Bulgaria.

actual.note: United Principality of Bulgaria (with Eastern Rumelia)

questions.conf_note: Well documented. OHM is simply missing the record.
why: OHM has no Bulgaria record between September 1885 and 1908.

questions.title: Eastern Rumelia 1878–1885
questions.question: Should self-governing Eastern Rumelia show as its own unit?
questions.problem: OHM shows Eastern Rumelia as a self-governing province. CShapes and Cliopatria show the Ottoman Empire.
questions.conf_note: Only the rule decides this one.
why: CShapes and Cliopatria do not record self-governing provinces.

questions.title: Kyustendil, Kardzhali and Smolyan
questions.question: Which side of the Bulgarian–Ottoman line were these three towns on after 1878?
questions.problem: CShapes puts Kyustendil in the Ottoman Empire. Cliopatria puts Kardzhali and Smolyan in Bulgaria.

legal.note: Kyustendil: Bulgaria from the Treaty of Berlin
Kardzhali: Ottoman under the Tophane Agreement

questions.conf_note: Kyustendil and Smolyan are clear. Who held Kardzhali between 1878 and 1886 needs an expert.
why: CShapes and Cliopatria draw this border coarsely.

questions.title: Ionian Islands 1815–1864
questions.question: Show the Ionian Islands as their own state, or as British?
questions.problem: OHM shows the United States of the Ionian Islands. CShapes and Cliopatria show the United Kingdom. Cliopatria also keeps the UK after the 1864 union with Greece.
questions.conf_note: Facts are clear. The rule decides how to show a protectorate.
why: OHM has no record for the islands before November 1815.
Cliopatria keeps a British claim on some islands until 1869.

questions.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina 1878–1900
questions.question: Ottoman (legal title) or Austro-Hungarian (actual control)?
questions.problem: OHM keeps Bosnia Ottoman. CShapes and Cliopatria show Austria-Hungary from 1878.
questions.conf_note: Both views are correct; the rule decides which map shows which.
why: Sources pick different kinds of control.

questions.title: Bay of Kotor 1815–1900
questions.question: Who held Kotor and Herceg Novi?
questions.problem: CShapes shows the Ottoman Empire until 1878 and Montenegro after. Cliopatria shows France until 1819. OHM shows Austria.
questions.conf_note: Austrian from the Congress of Vienna to 1918.
why: CShapes and Cliopatria draw the coast coarsely.

questions.title: Spič (Sutomore) after 1878
questions.question: Who held the Spič coast after 1878?
questions.problem: OHM shows Austria-Hungary. CShapes shows Montenegro. Cliopatria shows the Ottoman Empire, then Montenegro.

legal.note: Given to Austria-Hungary (Dalmatia) by the Treaty of Berlin

questions.conf_note: The Treaty of Berlin names Spizza explicitly.
why: A small strip that coarse sources miss.

questions.title: Zemun 1815–1900
questions.question: Was Zemun Serbian or Habsburg?
questions.problem: CShapes shows the Ottoman Empire, then Serbia. Cliopatria shows Serbia. OHM shows Austria.

legal.note: Habsburg border town across the river from Belgrade

questions.conf_note: Habsburg until 1918.
why: Zemun sits across the river from Belgrade; coarse borders put it on the wrong side.

questions.title: Turnu Severin 1815–1900
questions.question: Was Turnu Severin in Wallachia or Serbia?
questions.problem: Cliopatria places it in Serbia. OHM and CShapes place it on the Wallachian (Romanian) side.
questions.conf_note: The town is on the north bank of the Danube, in Wallachia.
why: Cliopatria draws the Danube border coarsely.

questions.title: Suceava (Bukovina) 1815–1900
questions.question: Was Suceava Austrian or Moldavian?
questions.problem: Cliopatria places it in Moldavia, Russia or Romania at different times. OHM and CShapes show Austria.
questions.conf_note: Austrian from 1775 to 1918.
why: Cliopatria draws the Bukovina border coarsely.

questions.title: Montenegro before 1878
questions.question: Show Montenegro as independent before the powers recognized it in 1878?
questions.problem: OHM shows Montenegro throughout. CShapes shows the Ottoman Empire until 1878. Cliopatria shows the Ottoman Empire until 1852.

actual.note: Self-ruling under its prince-bishops, a principality from 1852

questions.conf_note: Facts are clear; the rule decides which map shows which.
why: Sources pick different kinds of control.

questions.title: When did Nikšić, Podgorica, Bar, Kolašin and Ulcinj become Montenegrin?
questions.question: When did each of these towns become Montenegrin?
questions.problem: OHM puts Ulcinj in Montenegro in 1878, two years early. Cliopatria shows Nikšić and Kolašin as Montenegrin from 1853 and keeps Podgorica, Bar, Ulcinj and Andrijevica Ottoman until 1885.

legal.note: Nikšić, Podgorica, Bar, Andrijevica (Treaty of Berlin)

questions.conf_note: Ulcinj, Podgorica and Kolašin are documented. Andrijevica needs checking.
why: OHM gives Ulcinj the 1878 date of the other towns.
Cliopatria uses the wrong decades.

questions.title: When does Greece begin?
questions.question: From which date should the Greek state show: 1822, 1830 or 1832?
questions.problem: OHM starts Greece in May 1832 (with an Ottoman overlap until August). CShapes starts in 1829–31. Cliopatria starts some towns in 1822 and wrongly includes Crete in 1828–29.

legal.note: Independence recognized by the London Protocol; borders fixed in 1832

actual.note: Greek provisional government in much of the Peloponnese from 1822, with reconquests in 1825–27

questions.conf_note: The legal dates are clear. Actual control in the 1820s changed town by town and needs an expert.
why: OHM uses the final 1832 borders only.
Cliopatria extends Greece to Crete for 1828–29, which is wrong.

questions.title: Crete under Egypt 1830–1840
questions.question: Show Egyptian rule over Crete (1830–1840) as its own holder?
questions.problem: OHM and CShapes show Egypt. Cliopatria shows the Ottoman Empire, and Greece for 1831–33.

actual.note: Governed by Muhammad Ali of Egypt

questions.conf_note: Cliopatria's Greek period is an error; the rest is the rule.
why: Cliopatria gives Crete to Greece for 1831–33 by mistake.

questions.title: Cretan State from 1898
questions.question: Show the self-governing Cretan State as its own unit?
questions.problem: OHM and Cliopatria show the Cretan State. CShapes shows the Ottoman Empire.
questions.conf_note: OHM gives only the year (1898); the new state began in December.
why: CShapes records only fully independent states.

questions.title: Thessaly, Arta and Tyrnavos after 1881
questions.question: When did Thessaly, Arta and Tyrnavos become Greek?
questions.problem: OHM leaves Arta and Tyrnavos Ottoman. CShapes keeps Tyrnavos Ottoman. Cliopatria keeps Larissa, Volos and Trikala Ottoman until 1885.

legal.note: Handed over after the Convention of Constantinople

questions.conf_note: The 1881 convention names these districts.
why: OHM's 1881 border is drawn wrong at Arta and Tyrnavos.
Cliopatria moves the change to 1885.

questions.title: Elassona and Preveza
questions.question: Were Elassona and Preveza Greek before 1900?
questions.problem: Cliopatria puts both towns in Greece from 1834. OHM and CShapes keep them Ottoman.
questions.conf_note: The 1881 border left both towns outside Greece.
why: Cliopatria draws the Greek border too far north.

questions.title: No country anywhere in the Ottoman lands in 1897
questions.question: Who held the Ottoman lands in 1897?
questions.problem: OHM ends one Ottoman record in "1897" and starts the next in "1898", leaving the whole year empty.

legal.note: Ottoman Empire continuously; the Dec 1897 treaty moved only small border strips

questions.conf_note: A data gap in OHM, not a historical question.
why: Year-only dates in OHM leave a gap.

questions.title: Southern Bessarabia 1849–1856
questions.question: Russian or Ottoman before the 1856 transfer?
questions.problem: CShapes shows Russia and the Ottoman Empire at the same time. OHM and Cliopatria show Russia.

legal.note: Transferred to Moldavia by the Treaty of Paris

questions.conf_note: The Treaty of Paris dates the change.
why: CShapes has overlapping records here.

questions.title: Ruse and Silistra
questions.question: Were Ruse and Silistra on the Ottoman or the Wallachian side?
questions.problem: Cliopatria places both towns in Wallachia or Romania, and in some years Russia or Austria. OHM and CShapes keep them Ottoman until 1878.
questions.conf_note: Both towns are on the south bank of the Danube. Russian troops held Silistra for a time after 1829; that belongs to the actual-control map.
why: Cliopatria draws the Danube border on the wrong side.

questions.title: Novi Pazar, Pljevlja and Bijelo Polje after 1878
questions.question: Who held the Sanjak of Novi Pazar after 1878?
questions.problem: CShapes puts Novi Pazar in Serbia. Cliopatria puts Pljevlja and Bijelo Polje in Austria-Hungary.

legal.note: Ottoman, with Austro-Hungarian garrisons allowed from 1879

questions.conf_note: The garrisons did not change who ruled the area.
why: CShapes and Cliopatria confuse garrisons with rule.

questions.title: Transylvania and Banat 1849–1852
questions.question: Did the Hungarian revolutionaries hold the area until 1852?
questions.problem: Cliopatria shows Hungarian revolutionaries until 1852. OHM and CShapes show Austria.
questions.conf_note: The revolution ended in August 1849.
why: Cliopatria carries the revolution on for three years too long.

questions.title: Russian administration of Bulgaria 1877–1879
questions.question: Show the Russian provisional administration on the actual-control map?
questions.problem: Cliopatria shows Russia for 1877–79. OHM and CShapes show the Ottoman Empire, then Bulgaria.
questions.conf_note: The end date differs between Bulgaria proper and Eastern Rumelia.
why: Sources pick different kinds of control.

serbia1830.title: Ottoman decrees of 1830 and 1833 on Serbian self-rule

hungary1849.title: End of the Hungarian revolution (surrender at Világos)

london1864.title: Treaty of London (1864): Ionian Islands to Greece

bosnia1878.title: Austro-Hungarian occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

constantinople1881.title: Convention of Constantinople (1881): Thessaly and Arta to Greece

tyrnavos.title: Tyrnavos annexed with the rest of Thessaly

dalmatia.title: Kingdom of Dalmatia (Austrian, incl. Bay of Kotor)

frontier.title: Military Frontier (Habsburg border zone incl. Zemun)

rules.q: How should self-governing states under an overlord be shown?
rules.why: Serbia, Wallachia, Moldavia, Bulgaria, Eastern Rumelia, the Ionian Islands and Crete governed themselves but were not fully independent.
options: As their own states, marked self-governing

rules.q: Which kind of control does the main map show?
rules.why: Bosnia, Montenegro, the occupied principalities and 1877–79 Bulgaria were held legally by one state and actually by another.

rules.q: When sources agree who, but differ by a year on when, what counts?
rules.why: Sources use whole years differently; OHM usually has the exact day.
options: Use the most precise date (usually OHM) automatically

rules.why: Reviewers do not need to be historians if the evidence is strong enough.
options: Anyone, when every change date links to a treaty or event
